title: Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
authors: Chunjing Jia, Valentin Walther, Laimei Nie
abstract: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) is conventionally used to probe elementary excitations and correlations in quantum materials. Here, we propose an interferometric RIXS protocol that instead creates entanglement between spatially separated regions of a solid-state material. An incident X-ray photon is coherently split by a beam splitter into two arms illuminating opposite ends of a sample. Recombining the scattered photons at a second beam splitter and detecting an energy-selected photon then projects the material into a coherent superposition of excitations at the two ends. This protocol is the X-ray, solid-state analogue of the Duan-Lukin-Cirac-Zoller (DLCZ) heralding scheme. Using a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism with quantized photon modes, we show that orthogonal and degenerate end excitations yield maximally entangled states. We illustrate this mechanism in three models: (1) two decoupled sites yield a heralded Bell state. (2) An open tight-binding chain exhibits reflection-parity-dependent interference, providing a benchmark for the interferometer's coherence. (3) A spin-1 Haldane (AKLT) chain yields an entangled pair of fractionalized edge spins. We also discuss practical considerations and challenges for realizing the protocol in X-ray experiments.
summary: The authors propose an interferometric RIXS technique to generate entanglement across spatially separated parts of a quantum material. By splitting and recombining X-ray photons, the process projects the material into a coherent superposition of excitations. This method successfully demonstrates entanglement generation in the Haldane chain, offering a powerful new diagnostic tool for studying quantum correlations in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: To generate and detect entanglement between spatially separated regions of a solid-state material using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS).
main_result: The proposed interferometric RIXS protocol successfully generates heralded entangled states, reaching an entanglement entropy of $2\ln 2$ in the Haldane chain, significantly higher than conventional measurements.
method: The method involves using a Mach-Zehnder interferometer setup with X-ray photons, analyzing the resulting count rates ($I_{10} - I_{01}$) via a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism.
model_or_system: The study applies the protocol to several models, including two decoupled sites, an open tight-binding chain, and the spin-1 Haldane (AKLT) chain, which serves as the primary interacting system.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy ($S$), difference in count rates ($I_{10} - I_{01}$), and local magnetization ($\langle S^z_j angle$).
important_parameters: The relative phase $\Phi$ between the two interferometer arms, and the gap ($\Delta_H$) separating spin-flip excitations from bulk excitations.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes coherence between the two interferometer arms and ideal energy selection capabilities of the analyzer.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the two-site limit, parity-dependent routing in the tight-binding chain, and a comparison of entanglement entropy for the AKLT chain, showing the increase to $2\ln 2$ for the heralded state.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the interferometric RIXS protocol, derives the state evolution using the Kramers-Heisenberg formalism, analyzes the results in the two-site limit, extends the analysis to the tight-binding chain, and finally demonstrates entanglement generation in the Haldane chain.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum optics (interferometry, photon entanglement) with condensed matter physics (spin chains, correlated materials), providing a novel, non-destructive spectroscopic tool to probe quantum correlations in solids.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Pathway-entangled-photon RIXS on a one- dimensional sample. The incident mode a1 is coherently di- vided by a 50/50 beam splitter A into arms b1 and b2, which are focused on the two ends j = 1 and j = N of the chain (gray box; the two illuminated end sites are shown in blue). The scattered modes s1, s2 are recombined on a second 50/50 splitter B and registered by detectors d1, d2. In the energy- resolved configuration analyzed in the main text, an energy analyzer in each arm (not drawn) transmits only the inelas- tically scattered photon at ℏωout = ℏωin −ℏωloss, so that a single click at d1 or d2 heralds the prepared state.

Figure 2. The two-site limit of Fig. 1. The sample is reduced to two decoupled sites, each placed under an optical pathway. An excitation created at site 1 cannot propagate, so the two ends feed the orthogonal, degenerate final states |eg⟩and |ge⟩. This is the solid-state counterpart of the two atomic ensembles of the DLCZ protocol [15], with the two illuminated sites playing the role of the ensembles and the core-hole resonance playing the role of the Raman drive.
